title.narrative: Addressing the multi-sectoral needs of the most vulnerable persons during the lean season in conflict-affected locations in Borno State.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project will address specialized Child protection and Gender-based violence needs and gaps across one conflict-affected local government area of Damasak- Mobbar LGA in Borno State Northeast Nigeria. It will build on completed Protection and Education in emergency projects in areas where Street Child has a long-established presence. Through coordinating with our local partner Protection without Borders League (POWIB) we will deliver an integrated holistic set of activities that draw on our collective strengths in Child Protection and Gender Based Violence programming.ltbrgtStreet Child and POWIB are all experienced partner with good experience working across the Northeast on Child Protection and GBV projects and together have implemented the lean season 1st reserve allocation in 2023 in same proposed locations of Damasak- Mobbar LGA of Borno StateltbrgtDrawing on our long experience managing the consortium, Street Child will provide oversight and capacity building support to our partners whilst providing a range of feedback mechanisms to ensure that all our work is accountable to the local population. The partnership will work out of the same facilities and communities to ensure we benefit from regular contact through cross referrals, complementing with other partners, service provision and tracked progress whilst easing the time and cost of referrals. Street Child will also run training with staff, partners and locally contracted volunteers on a range this in informed based on our documented lesson learned from previous NHF funded project on the 1st reserve allocation NGO consortium in 2021. ltbrgtIn addition to our coordination role, Street Child will provide specialized services to complement our partners’ activities. Through responding to our partners’ case management referrals, we will provide cash support to high-risk beneficiaries, Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR) services to unaccompanied children including the provision of alternative care facilities or transport to reunify displaced family members. Parenting programmes to foster carers or other caregivers will be built on and rolled out to new attendees of our nutrition partner’s work. Children identified at risk including GBV survivors through our partners Psychosocial Support and life skills training will be referred to our Mental Health Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) specialist who can provide support, counselling and dedicated psychological assistance including referrals for tier 4 services.ltbrgtTo ensure our partners’ case management services provided are comprehensive, referral pathways will be mapped out (if not already available) and strengthened through advocacy and coordination with the relevant clusters at the community and LGA level. ltbrgtFinally, Street Child will use their experience of building the technical and organizational capacity of local partners to develop a strong capacity support plan. This will involve mainstreaming protection issues through training on PSEA, GBV, Disability inclusion and child safeguarding, developing responsive monitoring activities that encourage active participation from our attendees and creating shared CRM systems that hold us accountable to the local population. Through involving of government authority across Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development, Primary health care and Ministry of Health representatives and social workers in all trainings and field activities will also promote government buy-in and strengthen government capacity on ownership and sustainability.ltbrgtlt/pgt
